verses.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν Ἰκονίῳ κατὰ τὸ αὐτὸ εἰσελθεῖν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν συναγωγὴν τῶν Ἰουδαίων καὶ λαλῆσαι οὕτως ὥστε πιστεῦσαι Ἰουδαίων τε καὶ Ἑλλήνων πολὺ πλῆθος
verses.transliteration: Egeneto de en Ikoniō kata to auto eiselthein autous eis tēn synagōgēn tōn Ioudaiōn kai lalēsai houtōs hōste pisteusai Ioudaiōn te kai Hellēnōn poly plēthos
verses.literal: At Iconium Paul and Barnabas went as usual . . . . . . into the Jewish synagogue where they spoke so well that a great number of Jews and Greeks believed

verses.original: οἱ δὲ ἀπειθήσαντες Ἰουδαῖοι ἐπήγειραν καὶ ἐκάκωσαν τὰς ψυχὰς τῶν ἐθνῶν κατὰ τῶν ἀδελφῶν
verses.transliteration: hoi de apeithēsantes Ioudaioi epēgeiran kai ekakōsan tas psychas tōn ethnōn kata tōn adelphōn
verses.literal: But the unbelieving Jews stirred up the Gentiles and poisoned their minds against the brothers

verses.original: ἱκανὸν μὲν οὖν χρόνον διέτριψαν παρρησιαζόμενοι ἐπὶ τῷ Κυρίῳ τῷ μαρτυροῦντι ἐπὶ τῷ λόγῳ τῆς χάριτος αὐτοῦ διδόντι σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα γίνεσθαι διὰ τῶν χειρῶν αὐτῶν
verses.transliteration: hikanon men oun chronon dietripsan parrēsiazomenoi epi tō Kyriō tō martyrounti epi tō logō tēs charitos autou didonti sēmeia kai terata ginesthai dia tōn cheirōn autōn
verses.literal: So Paul and Barnabas spent considerable time there speaking boldly for the Lord who affirmed . . . the message of His grace by enabling them to perform signs and wonders

verses.original: Ἐσχίσθη δὲ τὸ πλῆθος τῆς πόλεως καὶ οἱ μὲν ἦσαν σὺν τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις οἱ δὲ σὺν τοῖς ἀποστόλοις
verses.transliteration: Eschisthē de to plēthos tēs poleōs kai hoi men ēsan syn tois Ioudaiois hoi de syn tois apostolois
verses.literal: The people of the city were divided - Some sided with the Jews and others with the apostles

verses.original: ὡς δὲ ἐγένετο ὁρμὴ τῶν ἐθνῶν τε καὶ Ἰουδαίων σὺν τοῖς ἄρχουσιν αὐτῶν ὑβρίσαι καὶ λιθοβολῆσαι αὐτούς
verses.transliteration: hōs de egeneto hormē tōn ethnōn te kai Ioudaiōn syn tois archousin autōn hybrisai kai lithobolēsai autous
verses.literal: But when the Gentiles and Jews together with their rulers set out to mistreat and stone them

verses.original: συνιδόντες κατέφυγον εἰς τὰς πόλεις τῆς Λυκαονίας Λύστραν καὶ Δέρβην καὶ τὴν περίχωρον
verses.transliteration: synidontes katephygon eis tas poleis tēs Lykaonias Lystran kai Derbēn kai tēn perichōron
verses.literal: they found out about it and fled to the Lycaonian cities of Lystra and Derbe and to the surrounding region

verses.original: κἀκεῖ εὐαγγελιζόμενοι ἦσαν
verses.transliteration: kakei euangelizomenoi ēsan
verses.literal: where they continued to preach the gospel

verses.original: Καί τις ἀνὴρ ἀδύνατος ἐν Λύστροις τοῖς ποσὶν ἐκάθητο χωλὸς ἐκ κοιλίας μητρὸς αὐτοῦ ὃς οὐδέποτε περιεπάτησεν
verses.transliteration: Kai tis anēr adynatos en Lystrois tois posin ekathēto chōlos ek koilias mētros autou hos oudepote periepatēsen
verses.literal: In Lystra there sat a man crippled in his feet who was lame from . . . . . . birth and had never walked

verses.original: οὗτος ἤκουσεν τοῦ Παύλου λαλοῦντος ὃς ἀτενίσας αὐτῷ καὶ ἰδὼν ὅτι ἔχει πίστιν τοῦ σωθῆναι
verses.transliteration: houtos ēkousen tou Paulou lalountos hos atenisas autō kai idōn hoti echei pistin tou sōthēnai
verses.literal: This man was listening to the words of Paul who looked intently at him and saw that he had faith to be healed

verses.original: εἶπεν μεγάλῃ φωνῇ Ἀνάστηθι ἐπὶ τοὺς πόδας σου ὀρθός καὶ ἥλατο καὶ περιεπάτει
verses.transliteration: eipen megalē phōnē Anastēthi epi tous podas sou orthos kai hēlato kai periepatei
verses.literal: In a loud voice Paul called out Stand up on your feet And the man jumped up and began to walk

verses.original: Οἵ τε ὄχλοι ἰδόντες ὃ ἐποίησεν Παῦλος ἐπῆραν τὴν φωνὴν αὐτῶν Λυκαονιστὶ λέγοντες Οἱ θεοὶ ὁμοιωθέντες ἀνθρώποις κατέβησαν πρὸς ἡμᾶς
verses.transliteration: Hoi te ochloi idontes ho epoiēsen Paulos epēran tēn phōnēn autōn Lykaonisti legontes Hoi theoi homoiōthentes anthrōpois katebēsan pros hēmas
verses.literal: When the crowds saw what Paul had done they lifted up their voices in the Lycaonian language The gods have come down to us in human form . . .

verses.original: ἐκάλουν τε τὸν Βαρνάβαν Δία τὸν δὲ Παῦλον Ἑρμῆν ἐπειδὴ αὐτὸς ἦν ὁ ἡγούμενος τοῦ λόγου
verses.transliteration: ekaloun te ton Barnaban Dia ton de Paulon Hermēn epeidē autos ēn ho hēgoumenos tou logou
verses.literal: Barnabas they called Zeus and Paul they called Hermes because he was the chief speaker

verses.original: ὅ τε ἱερεὺς τοῦ Διὸς τοῦ ὄντος πρὸ τῆς πόλεως ταύρους καὶ στέμματα ἐπὶ τοὺς πυλῶνας ἐνέγκας σὺν τοῖς ὄχλοις ἤθελεν θύειν
verses.transliteration: ho te hiereus tou Dios tou ontos pro tēs poleōs taurous kai stemmata epi tous pylōnas enenkas syn tois ochlois ēthelen thyein
verses.literal: The priest of Zeus whose temple was just outside the city brought bulls and wreaths to the city gates hoping to offer a sacrifice along with the crowds

verses.original: Ἀκούσαντες δὲ οἱ ἀπόστολοι Βαρνάβας καὶ Παῦλος διαρρήξαντες τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτῶν ἐξεπήδησαν εἰς τὸν ὄχλον κράζοντες
verses.transliteration: Akousantes de hoi apostoloi Barnabas kai Paulos diarrēxantes ta himatia autōn exepēdēsan eis ton ochlon krazontes
verses.literal: But when the apostles Barnabas and Paul found out about this they tore their clothes and rushed into the crowd shouting

verses.original: καὶ λέγοντες Ἄνδρες τί ταῦτα ποιεῖτε καὶ ἡμεῖς ὁμοιοπαθεῖς ἐσμεν ὑμῖν ἄνθρωποι εὐαγγελιζόμενοι ὑμᾶς ἀπὸ τούτων τῶν ματαίων ἐπιστρέφειν ἐπὶ θεὸν ζῶντα ὃς ἐποίησεν τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν καὶ τὴν θάλασσαν καὶ πάντα τὰ ἐν αὐτοῖς
verses.transliteration: kai legontes Andres ti tauta poieite kai hēmeis homoiopatheis esmen hymin anthrōpoi euangelizomenoi hymas apo toutōn tōn mataiōn epistrephein epi theon zōnta hos epoiēsen ton ouranon kai tēn gēn kai tēn thalassan kai panta ta en autois
verses.literal: Men why are you doing this We too are only men human like you We are bringing you good news . . . that you should turn from these worthless things to the living God who made heaven and earth and sea and everything in them

verses.original: ὃς ἐν ταῖς παρῳχημέναις γενεαῖς εἴασεν πάντα τὰ ἔθνη πορεύεσθαι ταῖς ὁδοῖς αὐτῶν
verses.transliteration: hos en tais parōchēmenais geneais eiasen panta ta ethnē poreuesthai tais hodois autōn
verses.literal: In past generations He let all nations go their own way

verses.original: καίτοι οὐκ ἀμάρτυρον αὑτὸν ἀφῆκεν ἀγαθουργῶν οὐρανόθεν ὑμῖν ὑετοὺς διδοὺς καὶ καιροὺς καρποφόρους ἐμπιπλῶν τροφῆς καὶ εὐφροσύνης τὰς καρδίας ὑμῶν
verses.transliteration: kaitoi ouk amartyron hauton aphēken agathourgōn ouranothen hymin hyetous didous kai kairous karpophorous empiplōn trophēs kai euphrosynēs tas kardias hymōn
verses.literal: Yet He has not left Himself without testimony to His goodness He gives you rain from heaven and fruitful seasons filling your hearts with food and gladness

verses.original: Καὶ ταῦτα λέγοντες μόλις κατέπαυσαν τοὺς ὄχλους τοῦ μὴ θύειν αὐτοῖς
verses.transliteration: Kai tauta legontes molis katepausan tous ochlous tou mē thyein autois
verses.literal: Even with these words Paul and Barnabas could hardly stop the crowds from sacrificing to them

verses.original: Ἐπῆλθαν δὲ ἀπὸ Ἀντιοχείας καὶ Ἰκονίου Ἰουδαῖοι καὶ πείσαντες τοὺς ὄχλους καὶ λιθάσαντες τὸν Παῦλον ἔσυρον ἔξω τῆς πόλεως νομίζοντες αὐτὸν τεθνηκέναι
verses.transliteration: Epēlthan de apo Antiocheias kai Ikoniou Ioudaioi kai peisantes tous ochlous kai lithasantes ton Paulon esyron exō tēs poleōs nomizontes auton tethnēkenai
verses.literal: Then some Jews arrived from Antioch and Iconium and won over the crowds They stoned Paul and dragged him outside the city presuming he was dead

verses.original: κυκλωσάντων δὲ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτὸν ἀναστὰς εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὴν πόλιν Καὶ τῇ ἐπαύριον ἐξῆλθεν σὺν τῷ Βαρνάβᾳ εἰς Δέρβην
verses.transliteration: kyklōsantōn de tōn mathētōn auton anastas eisēlthen eis tēn polin Kai tē epaurion exēlthen syn tō Barnaba eis Derbēn
verses.literal: But after the disciples had gathered around him he got up and went back into . . . the city And the next day he left with Barnabas for Derbe

verses.original: Εὐαγγελισάμενοί τε τὴν πόλιν ἐκείνην καὶ μαθητεύσαντες ἱκανοὺς ὑπέστρεψαν εἰς τὴν Λύστραν καὶ εἰς Ἰκόνιον καὶ εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν
verses.transliteration: Euangelisamenoi te tēn polin ekeinēn kai mathēteusantes hikanous hypestrepsan eis tēn Lystran kai eis Ikonion kai eis Antiocheian
verses.literal: They preached the gospel to that city and made many disciples . . . Then they returned to Lystra - Iconium and Antioch

verses.original: ἐπιστηρίζοντες τὰς ψυχὰς τῶν μαθητῶν παρακαλοῦντες ἐμμένειν τῇ πίστει καὶ ὅτι Διὰ πολλῶν θλίψεων δεῖ ἡμᾶς εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ
verses.transliteration: epistērizontes tas psychas tōn mathētōn parakalountes emmenein tē pistei kai hoti Dia pollōn thlipseōn dei hēmas eiselthein eis tēn basileian tou Theou
verses.literal: strengthening the souls of the disciples and encouraging them to continue in the faith We must endure many hardships to enter . . . the kingdom of God they said

verses.original: Χειροτονήσαντες δὲ αὐτοῖς κατ’ ἐκκλησίαν πρεσβυτέρους προσευξάμενοι μετὰ νηστειῶν παρέθεντο αὐτοὺς τῷ Κυρίῳ εἰς ὃν πεπιστεύκεισαν
verses.transliteration: Cheirotonēsantes de autois kat’ ekklēsian presbyterous proseuxamenoi meta nēsteiōn parethento autous tō Kyriō eis hon pepisteukeisan
verses.literal: Paul and Barnabas appointed elders for them in each church praying and fasting as they entrusted them to the Lord in whom they had believed

verses.original: Καὶ διελθόντες τὴν Πισιδίαν ἦλθον εἰς τὴν Παμφυλίαν
verses.transliteration: Kai dielthontes tēn Pisidian ēlthon eis tēn Pamphylian
verses.literal: After passing through Pisidia they came to Pamphylia

verses.original: καὶ λαλήσαντες ἐν Πέργῃ τὸν λόγον κατέβησαν εἰς Ἀττάλειαν
verses.transliteration: kai lalēsantes en Pergē ton logon katebēsan eis Attaleian
verses.literal: And when they had spoken the word in Perga they went down to Attalia

verses.original: Κἀκεῖθεν ἀπέπλευσαν εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν ὅθεν ἦσαν παραδεδομένοι τῇ χάριτι τοῦ Θεοῦ εἰς τὸ ἔργον ὃ ἐπλήρωσαν
verses.transliteration: Kakeithen apepleusan eis Antiocheian hothen ēsan paradedomenoi tē chariti tou Theou eis to ergon ho eplērōsan
verses.literal: From Attalia they sailed to Antioch where they had been commended to the grace of God for the work they had just completed

verses.original: Παραγενόμενοι δὲ καὶ συναγαγόντες τὴν ἐκκλησίαν ἀνήγγελλον ὅσα ἐποίησεν ὁ Θεὸς μετ’ αὐτῶν καὶ ὅτι ἤνοιξεν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν θύραν πίστεως
verses.transliteration: Paragenomenoi de kai synagagontes tēn ekklēsian anēngellon hosa epoiēsen ho Theos met’ autōn kai hoti ēnoixen tois ethnesin thyran pisteōs
verses.literal: When they arrived they gathered the church together and reported all that God had done through them and how He had opened the door of faith to the Gentiles

verses.original: διέτριβον δὲ χρόνον οὐκ ὀλίγον σὺν τοῖς μαθηταῖς
verses.transliteration: dietribon de chronon ouk oligon syn tois mathētais
verses.literal: And they spent a long time there with the disciples
